en.name: Dried scallop
en.summary: Conpoy is the adductor muscle of the scallop, salted and dried hard until it is amber and intensely savoury. Airtight in a cool dry cupboard it keeps 6–12 months; refrigerated about 12 months, and frozen about 24 months. Most households refrigerate it simply because it is expensive.
en.pantry: Keep conpoy airtight, cool, dry and dark, and it runs 6–12 months. That figure sits at the long end of the general dried-food range because conpoy is dried much harder and is far less oily than dried shrimp; no agency publishes a number for it. The rule for dry goods is a sealed or covered container somewhere cool and dry, and glass lets you see if moisture has got in. A white bloom of amino-acid crystals on the surface is normal and is part of why it tastes the way it does; fuzzy grey or green mould is not.
en.fridge: A sealed jar in the fridge is the standard practice for good conpoy — about 12 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below — and it is what most households do, partly because the stuff is expensive and partly because a humid kitchen is hard on any dried seafood. This figure is ordinary practice rather than a published one. Let the jar come up to room temperature before you open it, so condensation does not settle on the scallops. Once soaked, treat rehydrated conpoy and its precious soaking liquid as fresh cooked seafood and use both within a couple of days.
en.freezer: Frozen, conpoy keeps about 24 months at −18 °C (0 °F) — again ordinary practice rather than a published figure. Freeze the sealed jar or a double-bagged portion, and bring it back to room temperature before opening, for the same condensation reason. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the timeline is about aroma, which is the whole reason you bought conpoy rather than fresh scallops.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container to room temperature before opening, then use the scallops dry or soak them as usual. Do not thaw them uncovered in a warm kitchen.
spoilage: Fuzzy grey, green or black mould — different from the normal white crystalline bloom.
A musty or sour smell instead of a deep savoury-sweet one.
Scallops gone soft, tacky or damp rather than rock hard.
A rancid or fishy-sharp note, or a dull grey-brown colour.
tips: Store in glass so you can see any moisture.
Bring a cold jar to room temperature before opening it.
Keep the soaking liquid — it is the best part — and use it within a day or two.
Buy whole scallops rather than broken shreds if you plan to keep them a long time.

faq.a: About 6–12 months airtight in a cool dry cupboard, about 12 months refrigerated, and about 24 months frozen.
They do not have to be, but a sealed jar in the fridge is standard practice, especially in a humid climate.

faq.q: What is the white powder on dried scallops?
faq.a: Amino-acid crystals, a normal part of a well-dried conpoy and part of its flavour. Fuzzy grey or green growth is mould and is not.

faq.q: How long does soaked conpoy keep?
faq.a: Treat rehydrated scallops and their soaking liquid as fresh cooked seafood: refrigerate and use within a couple of days.

zh.name: 干貝
zh.summary: 干貝是扇貝的閉殼肌經鹽漬乾燥製成，硬實呈琥珀色，鮮味濃烈。密封放陰涼乾燥櫥櫃可放 6～12 個月；冷藏約 12 個月；冷凍約 24 個月。多數家庭會冷藏保存，單純因為它很貴。
zh.pantry: 密封、陰涼、乾燥、避光，大約可放 6～12 個月。這個數字落在乾貨通用區間的長端，因為干貝乾得比蝦米徹底、含油也少得多；沒有機構公告過它的數字。乾貨的通則是密封或加蓋容器放陰涼乾燥處，而玻璃罐讓你看得出有沒有受潮。表面析出的白色胺基酸結晶是正常的，也是它鮮味的來源之一；灰綠色的絨毛霉則不是。
zh.fridge: 好干貝的標準做法是密封罐放冰箱——4 °C 以下約 12 個月——多數家庭也都這樣做，一來它貴，二來潮濕的廚房對任何海產乾貨都不友善。這個數字是一般實務而非公告值。開罐前先讓罐子回到室溫，避免水氣凝在干貝上。泡發之後，請把泡發的干貝和那碗珍貴的泡發水都當成熟海鮮看待，兩者都要在一兩天內用完。
zh.freezer: 冷凍的話，干貝在 −18 °C 下大約可放 24 個月——同樣是一般實務而非公告值。連密封罐或雙層袋一起冷凍，開封前一樣先回到室溫，理由還是結露。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，期限講的是香氣，而香氣正是你買干貝而不是買鮮干貝的全部理由。
zh.thawing: 連容器回到室溫再開封，之後直接使用或照常泡發。不要在溫暖的廚房裡敞開解凍。
spoilage: 灰、綠或黑色的絨毛霉——和正常的白色結晶不同。
聞起來有霉味或酸味，而不是深沉的鮮甜香。
干貝變軟、發黏或潮濕，而不是硬實。
出現油耗或尖銳腥味，或顏色轉為暗灰褐。
tips: 用玻璃罐裝，才看得出有沒有受潮。
冰過的罐子先回溫再開。
泡發水是精華，請留下並在一兩天內用掉。
打算長期保存的話買整顆，不要買碎絲。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼乾燥櫥櫃約 6～12 個月，冷藏約 12 個月，冷凍約 24 個月。
不是非冷藏不可，但密封罐放冰箱是標準做法，在潮濕氣候下尤其如此。
是胺基酸結晶，乾燥良好的干貝本來就會有，也是鮮味來源之一。灰綠色的絨毛才是霉。

faq.q: 泡發的干貝可以放多久？
faq.a: 泡發後的干貝和泡發水都要當熟海鮮看待：冷藏並在一兩天內用完。
